correction.text: the four coastal valleys Huaura, Supe, Pativilca and Fortaleza, 150-200 km north of Lima

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -3100 to -1800: the page names four coastal valleys (Huaura, Supe, Pativilca, Fortaleza), Caral '150 to 200 km north of Lima' and 'only 1,800 km2' for the three principal valleys; a 60 km disc round Huacho, the Huaura river mouth, stands for the coast and valleys (about 11,000 km2, larger than the page's figure). Large-scale settlement is 'clearly apparent' from 3100 BCE in the lead.

region.text: the four coastal valleys Huaura, Supe, Pativilca and Fortaleza, 150-200 km north of Lima

ledger.note: c. 3100 BCE: the Norte Chico civilisation of the Supe, Pativilca and Fortaleza valleys takes shape. Large-scale settlement is 'clearly apparent' from 3100 BCE (lead; 3200 BCE in the body; the first city about 3500 BCE at Huaricanga); the Caral page has Caral developing between 3000 and 1800 BC and built c. 2600 BC.

region.text: the four coastal valleys Huaura, Supe, Pativilca and Fortaleza, 150-200 km north of Lima

ledger.note: c. 1800 BCE: the civilisation declines. 'The civilization began to decline c. 1800 BCE, as more powerful centers emerged elsewhere on the coast and in the Andes'; the Caral page says Caral was abandoned c. 2000 BC and a 2025 study links its abandonment to a drought around 2200 BCE. About a thousand years pass before Chavín.

sources.title: Norte Chico civilization
sources.note: Dates (4th-2nd millennia BCE), four valleys Huaura, Supe, Pativilca, Fortaleza, 1,800 km2 for three valleys, decline c. 1800 BCE, state question open.

sources.title: Caral
sources.note: Caral developed 3000-1800 BC, built c. 2600 BC, abandoned c. 2000 BC, Supe valley, 182 km north of Lima, 23 km from the coast.

notes: A culture; the page does not say whether it was a state ('sophisticated government is presumed to have been required') and does not call Caral a capital, so identity.capitals is empty. Dates differ by page: first city about 3500 BCE; settlement clear from 3100 or 3200 BCE; Caral built c. 2600 BC (Caral page; the page's 3000 BC start for the culture contradicts the 3100 BCE lead); abandonment c. 2000 BC (Caral page) against decline c. 1800 BCE (Norte Chico page) and a 2200 BCE drought. The disc round Huacho overstates the area (page: 1,800 km2 for three valleys). Caral is not a gazetteer place (gazetteer_names_needed: Caral, Supe valley). Chavín (900 BCE) follows after a gap of about 900 years.
